lesson_title: Your Phone Touched Six Countries Before You Did
hook_text: The phone in your hand has been to more countries than you have. Read it like a map.
clip_script: Take out your phone and read it like a map. The design might come from America or Korea. The chip: Taiwan. The screen: Korea or Japan. The cobalt in the battery: dug in the DRC, our neighbourhood. The assembly: China or Vietnam. The software updates: pulled down through an undersea cable that lands near Mtunzini on the KwaZulu-Natal coast. The airtime you buy from a spaza: sold by a company listed in Johannesburg and operating across Africa. One object, six countries minimum — that is globalisation, and you carry it daily.
visual_style: A phone exploding into labelled parts that fly to their spots on a spinning world map, ending with a cable rising out of the sea at the KZN coast.
pacing: Rapid part-by-part beats around the map, slowing for the undersea cable landing at home.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson: what built the one-world shop, who wins, who loses, and where South Africa stands.
